subject: Using tree objects and location objects instead of paths

messages.author: 8ca351cf93833dde
messages.subject: Using tree objects and location objects instead of paths
parts:
Hi Nick! 

I was wondering if there is a possibility to use directly a tree object instead of the path for the tree file to run BioGeoBEARS.
And the same for the locations, although this is less important because there's no problem for me to use the paths.

The thing is that I am trying to create a loop to run BioGeoBEARS in many different clades of a tree. So I import the tree at the beginning and then I extract each clade in R, so I have all the trees as separate objects (in which I will run BioGeoBEARS) but not as files in a directory. And to use those tree objects directly in BioGeoBEARS would be much more convenient than exporting them (write.tree) and using the file paths... Especially when there could be thousands of trees.

Thank you very much!

Hector

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Using tree objects and location objects instead of paths
parts:
Hi, 

This option doesn't exist in the code at present. My philosophy has been it's better to have all the file inputs and file outputs all together for a particular run. However, it's easy to auto-generate files in your loop script, give the tree files different names, etc.  

Key functions in addition to write.tree:

For creating directories, or character strings to describe directories/paths:
dir.create
paste0
BioGeoBEARS::addslash
BioGeoBEARS::slashslash
normalizePath

For numbering files with 0-padding so they sort correctly:

# make e.g. 0001
i =1
tmpi = sprintf("%05.0f", i)
tmpi

Cheers,
Nick
